title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
claim: A convex quadratic over a polytope attains its maximum at the vertices and its minimum in the interior, as a geometric picture.
layout: 1 panel: filled contour plot of a polygon with a side colorbar
description: A single filled-contour plot shows a convex pentagon-like region (the convex hull of 5 points) in the plane. Five vertices are marked with black crosses and the hull boundary is drawn as a black outline. Inside, the quadratic function 1/2<Bx,x> is shown with the plasma colormap. The values are dark purple near the center, with a nearly circular, slightly elliptical minimum of 0, and they grow smoothly through magenta and orange to bright yellow at the vertices. Concentric level sets make the bowl-shaped landscape clear. A vertical colorbar on the right is labeled with 1/2<Bx,x> and runs from 0.00 to about 0.48. The eye goes first to the dark center and then to the bright yellow corners. This shows that the function is largest at the extreme points.
caption: Plot of the quadratic x 7→ 1 2⟨Bx, x⟩with B = diag(1, 2), over the convex hull of 5 vertices.
abstract: We study the hardmax limit of self-attention dynamics for token embeddings obtained in the zero-temperature ($Î²\to+\infty$) regime, and relate it to the finite-$Î²$ setting. In this limit, the update rule can be viewed as a Frank-Wolfe step for a quadratic objective over the convex hull of the current token embeddings. When the key-query matrix is negative semidefinite, the method linearly contracts all tokens to a single cluster at the origin. When it is positive semidefinite, extending the hardmax rule to the entire convex hull induces a Voronoi diagram: vertices are stationary, interior points remain in their initial cells, and each token moves along a straight line toward its cell's vertex, yielding (super-)exponential convergence. As a byproduct, we also establish well-posedness of the associated ODE limit in this regime. Returning to the finite-$Î²$ regime, we model self-attention dynamics as a Markov chain and prove dynamic metastability: with high probability, interior tokens reach near-vertex configurations in a constant number of steps and remain within a small neighborhood for times that grow exponentially in the inverse temperature $Î²$, before ultimately collapsing to the origin. Thus, the hardmax dynamics accurately approximate the finite-$Î²$ process over exponentially long time horizons.
